name: Attachment Test for Relative Shellability
statement: Let $\Delta$ be a finite pure complex of nonnegative dimension in which every ridge belongs to at most two facets, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonempty facet-generated subcomplex. If $\Lambda$ is pure and shellable but no shelling starts at a chosen facet $\rho$, then $\Theta=(\Delta*\langle\rho\rangle)\cup(\Gamma*\Lambda)$ is shellable exactly when $\Gamma$ is shellable and $(\Delta,\Gamma)$ is relatively shellable.
proof: Shellings of $\Gamma$, $\Lambda$, and the relative pair concatenate to give sufficiency. Conversely, the links of $\rho$ and of any other facet of $\Lambda$ recover shellings of $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$. Because $\rho$ cannot start a shelling of $\Lambda$, every $\Gamma$ facet precedes each ridge-adjacent outside facet: otherwise a codimension-two prefix link is disconnected, with the missing mixed edge as its only possible bridge. Non-ridge-sharing consecutive facets commute, so all $\Gamma$ facets can be moved first; the remaining order is relative.
